_readme: Built from the NJ Division of Taxation Coefficients of Deviation, which measure
how far individual assessment-to-sale ratios stray from a town's own average.
A high score means the town assesses its homes consistently. A low score means
the roll is uneven, and that unevenness is the argument a tax appeal is built on.
The equalization ratio tells you whether a town assesses high or low.
This tells you whether it assesses FAIRLY. They are completely different
questions and only one of them is published in a form anyone can use.
Scored from the residential (class 2) segmented coefficient, weighted toward the
most recent year, with penalties for year to year volatility and for thin sales
samples. Anchored on the IAAO standard of 15 for residential property, so a good
score means genuinely good and not merely better than the town next door.
Keyed by 4 digit district code: 2 digit county plus 2 digit municipality,
which is the first four characters of any PAMS PIN.
source: NJ Division of Taxation, Measures of Property Assessment Uniformity
